elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: 11.6.1(c) requires "General Liability Insurance with a minimum limit of [***] and [***] in the aggregate"; the per-occurrence figure is redacted, so it cannot be confirmed to reach USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: The aggregate limit in 11.6.1(c) is likewise redacted ([***] in the aggregate); the amount cannot be verified against USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence sets professional liability (errors and omissions) at "a minimum limit of USD 1,000,000", below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted cyber and privacy liability limit is USD 2,000,000; nothing in the clause raises it to USD 5,000,000 where Harpoon processes Customer Data, and no processing-based trigger is drafted.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: 11.6.1(a) retained: "Worker's Compensation with statutory limits in compliance with the Worker's Compensation laws of the state or states in which the Party has employees in the United States (excluding Puerto Rico)." applies to each Party, including Harpoon.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: 11.6.2 retained: "Upon request by a Party, the other Party shall provide Certificates of Insurance evidencing compliance with this Section." — this covers the newly inserted coverages, which sit within Section 11.6.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "Harpoon shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a minimum limit of USD 1,000,000..." — mandatory ("shall"), correct coverage type, meets the USD 1M floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "...and cyber and privacy liability insurance with a minimum limit of USD 2,000,000." — exact coverage description and amount required by the fallback.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: one inserted sentence supplies both required coverages at the exact required limits, in mandatory form, on the Vendor (Harpoon).

Preferred level is not complete: E&O is USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, cyber is USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000, and the retained general liability limits are redacted so the USD 1M/2M CGL elements cannot be verified. Workers' compensation and certificates-on-request are already satisfied by retained 11.6.1(a) and 11.6.2.

Minimal: a single concise insertion within the existing Section 11.6 framework; no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no additional-insured, notice-of-cancellation or procedural extras, and no duplication of the existing certificates or insurer-rating mechanics.

Preserves intent: the mutual insurance architecture, A.M. Best rating requirement, additional-insured provision, clinical trial cover, occurrence/claims-made tail in 11.6.2 and AbbVie's self-insurance right all survive without contradiction; the new coverages fall naturally within "this Section" for certificate purposes, leaving no dangling term or cross-reference.

Drafting note (not a defect): the insertion sits after 11.6.1(c) but is not numbered; consider lettering it as 11.6.1(d) so the certificate obligation's reference to "compliance with this Section" and the list structure remain clean.
If the team wants the preferred position, the operative repairs are: raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and add a Customer Data-triggered cyber limit of USD 5,000,000.
